implementation_statement: Enterprise access control policy POL-02 and standards STD-02.1 to STD-02.4 (P06) apply to the FMICP, including the OT remote access standard. Procedures PRC-02.1 to PRC-02.5 cover provisioning, certification, privileged access, break-glass, and OT vendor sessions.

Seasonal crew lead and scout accounts are created from the seasonal hiring roster and expire at the contract end date. responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management

responsible_role: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Duties are separated between proposing irrigation schedules (planners), approving fertigation recipes and injection limits (fertigation supervisors), and changing PLC logic (engineers). evidence: EV-008 (SCADA role matrix); EV-007 (FMIS role matrix); EV-AC-5 (P07 AC-5 results)

implementation_statement: Security functions (role assignment, alarm suppression, interlock bypass, audit settings) are limited to the engineer and security administrator roles and require a second approver for interlock bypass.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management
implementation_statement: Administrators use separate non-privileged accounts for email and web access; privileged accounts are vaulted in PAM.

responsible_role: Director of Identity and Access Management

evidence: EV-003 (PAM session recordings); EV-036 (SIEM use case PAM-01)

implementation_statement: SSO locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. Control center HMIs lock the operator account after 5 failed attempts but never lock the shared alarm view, so alarms stay visible (safety design choice).
FMIS, SCADA HMI, and remote access gateway sign-in screens display the approved system use notification.

responsible_role: Director of Endpoint and Mobility Engineering
implementation_statement: Office workstations lock after 10 minutes. Control room HMIs lock the session after 15 minutes but keep the alarm summary visible; rugged tablets lock after 5 minutes.
FMIS web sessions end after 30 minutes of inactivity; remote access gateway sessions end after 8 hours or 30 minutes idle.

Remote access to OT goes through the OT remote access gateway (jump hosts in the OT DMZ) with MFA, approval per session, and session recording. Gap: integrators INT-4 and INT-5 still use their own remote tools at about 120 pump stations (POAM-004), and AQ-02 pivots are controlled through the manufacturer's cloud service with shared logins and no MFA (POAM-002).
evidence: EV-022 (Gateway session log); EV-AC-17 (remote tool discovery scan, P07 AC-17 results)

provider_if_inherited: CCP-05 Enterprise network and OT DMZ (SYS-05)

evidence: EV-020 (Wireless configuration standard, APN routing review)

responsible_role: Director of Endpoint and Mobility Engineering
implementation_statement: Rugged tablets used for tally and irrigation are enrolled in mobile device management with a passcode, encryption, and remote wipe. Gap: AQ-01 tablets are unmanaged and share logins until integration (POAM-023).
Use of external systems is limited by POL-05 and STD-05.2. Integrators may not connect laptops to OT networks except through the gateway or on site with a scanned, approved device.
POL-05 and STD-05.1 set awareness and role-based training requirements for the workforce, including OT operators and seasonal crew leads.

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training

evidence: EV-051 (Learning system completion report, phishing metrics)

provider_if_inherited: CCP-08 Human resources and workforce training
implementation_statement: OT operators and engineers complete role-based OT security training covering safe states, remote access rules, and change control. Gap: 22% of irrigation technicians and all INT-4 and INT-5 staff lack completion records (POAM-018).
STD-01.4 (audit logging) applies, including the OT logging profile for SCADA, PLC change events, and the gateway.

Logged events: SCADA operator commands, setpoint and schedule changes, recipe changes, interlock bypasses, alarm acknowledgments, engineering downloads, FMIS record edits and deletions, gateway sessions, and authentication events.
SCADA and FMIS audit records include user, time, source station, object (pump, pivot, zone, skid, or record), old and new values, and outcome.
Setpoint and recipe change records include the old and new values and the approving supervisor where approval is required.

control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures
implementation_statement: The SIEM alerts the SOC when a FMICP log source stops sending for 60 minutes; control center historians buffer 72 hours locally.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews FMICP security events 24x7 with OT use cases (unscheduled fertigation change, interlock bypass, PLC download outside a change window). Gap: logs from AQ-01 farm servers and the AQ-02 pivot cloud service are not collected, and passive OT monitoring covers 120 of 410 pump stations (POAM-005).
evidence: EV-037 (SOC review records); EV-036 (log source inventory); EV-AU-6 (P07 AU-6 results)

implementation_statement: Review, analysis, and reporting are integrated through SIEM case management.
SCADA, gateway, identity, and FMIS events are correlated in the SIEM with OT monitoring alerts.

control_name: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation
implementation_statement: SIEM search and reporting tools support investigations without changing original records.
SCADA servers, HMIs, and PLCs synchronize to OT time servers in the DMZ that take GNSS time with a terrestrial backup source.
Logs are stored in a write-once archive in a separate account readable only by the SOC.
Logs are kept 1 year online and 3 years in the archive, enough to cover H-2A record periods (3 years) and Produce Safety records (2 years).
SCADA servers, HMIs, gateway, and the data hub generate audit records and forward them to the SIEM through the OT DMZ collector.
STD-01.2 defines assessment and authorization for tier-1 systems, including OT assessment rules of engagement.
Internal Audit, with a co-sourced OT assessment firm, assesses the FMICP annually (P07).
Assessors are independent of the teams that design and run the controls; Internal Audit reports functionally to the audit committee.

responsible_role: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: Interconnections are documented in section 8 of the SSP with agreements. Gap: the AQ-02 pivot cloud service and INT-4 and INT-5 remote paths have no interconnection security terms (POAM-002; POAM-004).
Weaknesses are tracked in the POA&M (P07) with owners and dates and reviewed monthly by the GRC team.
The Chief Operating Officer is the authorizing official equivalent and made the 2026 decision to operate with conditions (section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring reports key metrics monthly: OT remote sessions outside the gateway, patch status, inventory coverage, open POA&M items.
STD-01.5 (configuration and change management) applies, with the OT change procedure PRC-01.4 for PLC logic, setpoints, and recipes.
Baselines exist for SCADA servers, HMIs, engineering workstations, and each PLC model; the approved PLC program library holds the current version for each pump station and skid.

control_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency
implementation_statement: Baseline compliance for OT Windows hosts is checked weekly by the OT configuration scanner in passive or credentialed mode.

PLC logic, setpoint limits, and fertigation recipes change only through PRC-01.4 with a ticket, test on the bench PLC, regional supervisor approval, and a post-change check. Gap: 6 of 40 sampled changes lacked approval records, all at INT-4 and INT-5 stations (POAM-006).

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: Changes are tested on bench PLCs and the SCADA test environment before deployment.
Each OT change has a security and safety impact review, including any effect on interlocks and backflow protection.
evidence: EV-016 (Impact review fields in change tickets)

implementation_statement: Only engineering roles can download PLC logic, and only from engineering workstations through PAM.
Settings follow the OT hardening standard. Gap: 3 pump station HMIs and 11 LoRaWAN gateways kept default credentials, and pivot panel modems run vendor default services (POAM-010; POAM-009).
Unneeded services and ports are disabled on SCADA servers and HMIs; allowlisting is planned for HMIs that cannot run EDR (POAM-014).
The OT asset inventory combines passive monitoring, the SCADA tag database, and field service records. Gap: the field device inventory is about 78% complete (POAM-008).
Inventory is updated when devices are installed, replaced, or removed through the field work order process.
STD-03.3 (contingency and disaster recovery) applies, with regional manual irrigation and freeze-protection procedures.

responsible_role: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: The FMICP contingency plan v3 covers loss of SCADA masters, a control center, the APN, the FMIS, and power, with manual operation and freeze-night staffing by region.
evidence: EV-050 (Contingency plan v3, regional freeze plans)

responsible_role: Vice President, Irrigation and Water Resources
implementation_statement: The plan is coordinated with packing site, cold-chain, and labor plans (P05 dependencies).

Transaction recovery: schedules and setpoints are reconciled against the FMIS irrigation plan and field readings after a restore.

Field devices authenticate to the APN with SIM credentials and to LoRaWAN with device keys. Gap: some legacy pivot panels accept unauthenticated commands from the APN segment (POAM-009).

SOC analysts and OT responders train annually, including an OT tabletop.

STD-04.2 (media protection and disposal) applies.

implementation_statement: Critical components identified: SCADA masters, freeze pump station PLCs, fertigation skid interlock controllers.
OT and software purchases include security requirements (secure defaults, patch support, remote access through the gateway).

Company-built integrations (data hub, SCADA-to-FMIS interface) are tested with static and dynamic analysis before release.
